title: Installing Linux on Your Home Server
why: A home server gives you full control over your data and services. Linux is the ideal operating system for servers because it is free, open-source, extremely stable, and has excellent support for networking and server software. Ubuntu Server is a popular choice because of its long-term support (LTS) releases, large community, and straightforward installation process.

instructions.text: Download the Ubuntu Server ISO from the official website (https://ubuntu.com/download/server). Choose the latest LTS version for stability.
Create a bootable USB drive using a tool like Balena Etcher, Rufus (Windows), or the dd command on Linux.
instructions.command: sudo dd if=ubuntu-24.04-live-server-amd64.iso of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress
instructions.note: Replace /dev/sdX with your actual USB device. Be very careful to select the correct device — this will overwrite all data on it.

instructions.text: Insert the USB drive into your home server and boot from it. You may need to change the boot order in your BIOS/UEFI settings (usually accessed by pressing F2, F12, DEL, or ESC during boot).
Follow the Ubuntu Server installer. Choose your language, keyboard layout, and network configuration. For the disk setup, using the entire disk with LVM is recommended for flexibility.
Create your user account and set a strong password. Enable OpenSSH server when prompted — we will configure it further later.
After installation completes, remove the USB drive and reboot. Log in with the credentials you created.
Update the system to ensure all packages are current.
instructions.command: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

questions.text: Why is Linux preferred over Windows for a home server?
options: Linux is free, open-source, stable, and has excellent networking and server support
Linux comes pre-installed on most hardware
Linux does not require any updates

questions.text: What does the 'dd' command do when creating a bootable USB?
options: It downloads the ISO file from the internet
It formats the USB drive to NTFS
It copies the ISO image byte-by-byte to the USB device
It installs Linux directly onto the server

questions.text: Why is LVM recommended for disk setup?
options: It provides flexibility to resize partitions and manage storage later
It encrypts the entire disk automatically
It is the only option that Ubuntu supports
